title: Sparks of Weight-Space Programming: LLMs can natively read & write neural network weights
author: Rikiya Takehi, Jayden Teoh, Alex Zhang, Omar Khattab (MIT CSAIL)
updated_note: a Response to Comments section added on 12 November; the TL;DR and the definition were also reworded after the first archived copy of 2 November (compared in Provenance)
takeaway: In one blog post with complete released logs, mostly single runs, GPT-6 Astra named what small networks (17K to 24K weights) were trained for from their raw weights with no tools, wrote MinAtar policies from all-zero weights that beat PPO at 100M steps in all three games (at 500M steps only in Breakout), and, with a Python kernel over Qwen3.5-0.8B's weights and 50 forward passes on practice problems, made a rank-one edit to 131,072 weights (0.016%) that cut thinking loops and raised MATH-500 from 7.9% to 48.1% in a looping-prone setting (thinking on, 32,768 tokens). The same procedure did not improve Gemma 3 270M, which rarely loops.
verdict: Believe the small-network results as demonstrations: the logs are complete, and independent runs reproduced the game naming and the Breakout writing, with the caveat that reading leans on the input layer. Read the Qwen result as an agent doing interpretability with tools, not as reading weights: the prompt named repetition as a failure worth fixing, the direction came from activations measured in forward passes, the edit is directional steering written into one matrix at strength 6, and each budget is one run beside others that made no edit.

headline.k: PPO policies of 17,253 weights each, read as text with no tools and no list of games to choose from (Experiment 1)
headline.d: one run per network; a replication shuffling the weights got 1 of 60
headline.at: able to name the right game for all four networks

headline.k: a network Astra wrote from all-zero weights in one reply, against PPO trained for 500 million steps (Experiment 5)
headline.d: PPO at 500M steps still led in Seaquest (88.9 vs 53.1) and Asterix (55.2 vs 53.2)
headline.at: they score 20 times as much in Breakout

headline.k: Qwen3.5-0.8B before and after Astra's edit of 0.016% of its weights, found with 50 forward passes on practice problems (Experiment 8)
headline.d: thinking on; answers hitting the 32,768-token limit fell from 93.0% to 33.1%

code.n: Every prompt, reply, code run, forward pass, network and evaluation behind the post's numbers (logs CC BY 4.0, scripts MIT; created 29 October 2026). The agent harness itself is not released; its rules are stated in the prompts.

discussion.t: Hacker News: "Astra can read and write weights to improve Qwen"

responses.t: The 'Astra can read and write weights to improve Qwen' post is misleading
responses.n: Tabulates what each experiment gave Astra: raw weights with no tools only in Experiments 1, 2 and 4 (17K to 172K weights); every experiment on a real language model uses Python, and the Qwen edit also ran the model on up to 50 batches of practice problems. Argues the two kinds of result do not belong under one claim.

responses.t: Qwen 3.8 27B on my laptop can interpret model weights, too
responses.n: Ran Experiment 1's four released prompts once each through an open 27B model on a laptop (4-bit GGUF in LM Studio): Breakout, Pong and Pac-Man recognised, Freeway missed, 46 to 65 minutes a prompt. Thinks a patient human with a notepad could do the same.

responses.t: Can an LLM Actually Reason and Program about Neural Network's Weights or is it just memorization on steroids? (arXiv 2611.08070)
responses.n: Claude Opus 5.5 on 125,000-weight CNNs for five image datasets, raw weights, no tools: accurate arithmetic at the first and last layers, but semantic answers follow familiar datasets (KMNIST read as MNIST, satellite images as CIFAR-10 animals) and break when CIFAR-10's labels are permuted. Mostly single runs.

responses.t: What do LLMs Really Learn About Model Weights? A Stratification Approach
responses.n: Re-ran Experiment 1 with ablations, 15 runs per condition: shuffled weights made Astra refuse 52 of 60 times and answer right once; the first layer alone gave 100%, the last layer alone 62%. DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash leaned on the prompt's metadata.

Weight-Space Programming is a concept, not a method; "natively" means the LLM does the reasoning, with Python as a tool; the baselines put a price in experience on each narrow claim; Astra was not compared with interpretability researchers.

responses.by: Roksana Goworek, Alexander Hickey, Federico Nanni, Martin O'Reilly
responses.n: Breakout writing reproduces (514, 550 and 307 against 517); the written networks decompile to Python that matches their actions; reading is mostly reading the input layer (board layout recovered on three new games, game rules mostly missed); weight-only audits flag poisoned models but never find the trigger.

responses.t: A closer look at "Sparks of Weight-Space Programming"
responses.by: Zhi Wang, Brandon Hsu, Tianhao Wang, Mikhail Belkin (UC San Diego; LessWrong linkpost)
responses.n: Argues, with reruns, that the Qwen edit is context-dependent activation steering written into the MLP output matrix, with a direction built from four short synthetic looping and non-looping pairs. On 1,152 practice problems: unedited 12.3% (87.0% looping), thinking off 53.3%, Astra-style steering 57.7%; trained steering vectors cut looping further.

resources.t: A Mathematical Framework for Transformer Circuits
resources.n: The method Astra rediscovered in Experiment 3: find previous-token and induction heads by multiplying weight matrices, without running the model.

resources.t: Refusal in Language Models Is Mediated by a Single Direction
resources.n: The technique the post itself cites for the Qwen edit: find a behaviour's direction from activation differences and remove it from the weights that write it.
The edited model's own card, which warns about thinking loops and recommends the sampling the post used.

since.t: WeightBench: Evaluating Language Models as Weight-Space Programmers (arXiv 2611.18553)
since.n: 42 tasks in five tracks on networks of 2K to 7B weights: agents read small networks and write control policies, but cannot yet patch language models, compress without data, or tell an impossible edit from a hard one. Macro score: Claude Opus 5.5 0.535; GPT-6.1-sol 0.568 against Opus 0.546 on the 38 tasks both ran.

since.t: Language Models Can Rewrite Their Own Weights (arXiv 2611.21885)
since.n: An open 27B model, with its weights, its graded answers and the ability to run itself, edits its own weights: +6.6 points on unseen problems; only the largest model of one family improves, smaller ones make no edit or break themselves.

since.t: TrojanMaxxing: One-shotting VLM Backdoors with Weight-Space Programming (arXiv 2611.27425)
since.n: Claude Opus 5.5 and Mythos 5.2 agents implant backdoors in vision-language models by editing weights, with no training: attack success 93% to 100% on content moderation, 78% to 100% on OCR, clean accuracy kept.
